newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares finish mixed, blue chips firm.
newsitem.headline: KL shares finish mixed, blue chips firm.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur blue chips finished firmer in a quiet session on Thursday but smaller-capitalisation issues posted sharp losses after several days of run-ups.

"It's pretty quiet," said Tony Shue, a vice president in institutional sales at Jupiter Securities. "There's a fair bit of forced selling, and some buying from big institutions but they're pretty much bottom-fishing."
The Composite Index of 100 leading stocks closed up 9.29 points or 0.85 percent to 1,105.62. The Second Board ended down 9.33 points or 1.61 percent to 569.57.
"Blue chips edged up further led by continued support for Telekom...," GK Goh Stockbrokers said in its commentary.

Telekom's 70-cent surge underpinned the bulk of the Composite Index's gains. The telecommunications stock rose 70 cents to 18.80 ringgit, adding on to a 1.10 ringgit jump in the previous two sessions.
Buying ahead of the June 2 expiry of a one-for-two bonus issue again helped the stock, dealers said.
Other key stocks which boosted the key index included Petronas Gas which rose 25 to 8.95, Sime Darby which was up 25 to 8.40 and UMW's 50-cent gain to 12.80.
